newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state to auction batteries firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state to auction batteries firm.

text.p: Egypt's official Holding Company for Chemical Industries said on Tuesday it would auction its 38 percent stake, equivalent to 34,200 shares, in batteries firm Chloride Egypt to one or more strategic investors.
In a published advertisment, the holding company said closing date for bids was at noon (1000 GMT) on Thursday, January 16, 1997.
Investors must accompany their bids with finanical guarantee equal to two percent of the total amount and Egypt's Commercial International Bank is handling the sale.
Chloride Egypt has a capital of nine million pounds ($2.6 million) divided into 9,000 shares. It manufactures automotive and industrial batteries.
An Arab investor owns 52 percent of the firm and the American University's Investment Fund owns the remaining 10 percent, the agents for the sale said.
The Arab investor had bought the stake from British firm Chloride Plc, they added.
The holding company said Chloride Egypt's financial year begins on April 1.
